Class FormatRouter

java.lang.Object
org.casserole.format.FormatRouter
public class FormatRouter extends Object
The FormatRouter type paints an assistant reply with the first matching handler. If no handler matches, the reply is flowed as a paragraph and then given VT100 line endings. VT100 is the terminal control set the chat shell paints with. LinkAnnotator then marks links in the finished text.

  • Constructor Details

    • FormatRouter

      public FormatRouter()
      The constructor creates a router with no handlers. A router with no handlers keeps the reply text, flows the paragraph, and normalizes line endings.

    • getHandlers

      public List<FormatHandler> getHandlers()
      The getHandlers method returns the registered handlers. The list is the live list, so a later change to it changes the router.
      Returns:
      The handlers in registration order.

    • format

      public FormatResult format(String raw, FormatContext ctx)
      The format method paints one assistant reply. If raw is null or empty, the method returns an empty FormatResult with body color on. A null context is replaced with a new FormatContext. The first handler whose detector matches paints the reply. The painted text is passed through LineDiscipline.toCrlf(String) and LineDiscipline.ensureTrailingCrlf(String). LinkAnnotator.annotate(String) then marks links, and the handler's body-color flag is kept. If no handler matches, ParagraphFlow.flow(String) flows the paragraph before the same line-ending and link steps. That unmatched result has body color on.
      Parameters:
      raw - The original assistant text.
      ctx - The render settings, or null to use a fresh FormatContext.
      Returns:
      The formatted result.
